questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the core idea of “Concurrency Design Practices” in standard C++?
options: A compiler extension is guaranteed by every C++ implementation.
One successful run proves that every input and platform is handled correctly.
Type rules and object lifetime do not matter once a program compiles.
Concurrency Design Practices should be applied using its documented preconditions, with version and edge cases checked.
questions.answer_key: Concurrency Design Practices should be applied using its documented preconditions, with version and edge cases checked.
questions.explanation: The syllabus topic is “Concurrency Design Practices”. Concurrency Design Practices should be applied using its documented preconditions, with version and edge cases checked.

questions.prompt: When practicing “Concurrency Design Practices”, which approach gives the strongest initial evidence?
options: Assume the compiler default and language version are the same everywhere.
Copy a longer program without identifying its inputs or outputs.
State the preconditions, trace a minimal example and test a boundary or failure case.
Remove warnings and only test the ordinary happy path.
questions.answer_key: State the preconditions, trace a minimal example and test a boundary or failure case.
questions.explanation: Focused experiments with stated assumptions provide more useful evidence than an unexplained successful run.

questions.prompt: What should you do if an example related to “Concurrency Design Practices” depends on standard-version or toolchain support?
options: Assume that syntax accepted by one compiler is portable ISO C++.
Check the language/tool reference and record the selected standard and implementation assumptions.
Treat all draft features as universally implemented.
Replace the standard-library requirement with a compiler-specific function without a note.
questions.answer_key: Check the language/tool reference and record the selected standard and implementation assumptions.
questions.explanation: Standard mode and feature support must be checked explicitly; the course marks newer and implementation-dependent facilities accordingly.
